plain: To make pain, trouble, or a burden lighter.

webster.text: To make light; but always in a figurative sense, as it is not applied to material objects.

example.quote: If we pass over the consideration of this subject so essential to the preservation of our liberties, and turn our eyes to the form of the government which the Convention have proposed to us, I apprehend that changing the prospect will not wholly alleviate our fears.—A few words on this head, will close the present letter.
example.cite: An Old Whig V, Philadelphia Independent Gazetteer, Nov. 1, 1787
